case_title: NAGARAJ v. STATE REP. BY INSPECTOR OF POLICE, SALEM TOWN, TAMIL NADU
aggravating_circumstances: Accused surrendered after 18 months, no warrants for arrest
mitigating_circumstances: No motive established, failure of police investigation
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were working together in a business. They checked in at a hotel on the same day. The accused locked the hotel room and left alone with the room key and did not return. Two days later, a room boy noticed a bad odor coming from the room. The room was opened the next day with a master key given by the manager, and the decomposed body of the victim was found in the room. Eighteen months later, the accused surrendered before the judicial magistrate. The accused allegedly voluntarily confessed to killing the victim, but in his statement under s.313 CrPC, he denied his complicity in the offence. The courts below convicted and sentenced the accused under s.302 IPC based on circumstantial evidence. The High Court was not correct in drawing an adverse inference against the accused because of what he stated or failed to state under s.313 CrPC. The investigation conducted by the police was not satisfactory. Both the prosecution and the High Court took the deposition of the room boy to be trustworthy, ignoring the fact that the room boy and the manager had access to the hotel room for three days before the body of the deceased was found. They had as much motive and opportunity to commit the crime as was attributed to the accused. The statement of these witnesses cannot be relied upon. The failure of the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt led to the accused being given the benefit of the doubt.
